_comment: Tier-2: GridIn::read with malformed input raises ExcInOutCondTrue / similar parser exception. Reads a deliberately-truncated mesh file; verifies the exception class and 'GridIn' string appear.MUTATION CONTROL (2026-08-07): MUTATION APPLIED AND IT DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE. The T2_MUTATE=1 hook is left in source.cpp so the negative result stays re-runnable, but NO _mutation recipe is declared: a declared recipe that survives reads as a defect rather than as the finding it is (same treatment as dune/point_indicator_selects_no_facet and febio/static_activation_ramp_shape_does_not_matter). Re-run by hand from the fixture directory after any harness run has built it: `T2_MUTATE=1 ./_build/prog`. The hook feeds the same GridIn a COMPLETE one-quad Gmsh mesh instead of the truncated header, so there is nothing malformed left to raise on. Measured 2026-08-07: the read succeeds and the program prints "ERROR: GridIn accepted truncated mesh" and exits 2 — and the fixture STILL PASSES, because its single expectation is "GridIn" and the fixture writes that word itself in BOTH branches ("GridIn raised: ..." on the exception path, "ERROR: GridIn accepted ..." on the success path). Nothing in expect_in_output comes from deal.II; the fixture would pass unchanged if the library printed nothing at all. The fix would be an expectation naming the measured value; it is deliberately NOT made here, because tuning a fixture until its mutation goes red is how a mutation control stops being evidence.
